Newton – Euler Equation

Euler's equation
•   In a rigid body rotating with angular velocity 𝜔 and with
   angula acceleration ሶ𝜔, the moment 𝑁, which must be
   acting on the body to cause this motion, is given by

   that captures the gyroscopic effect — crucial for spinning
   robot joints and fast manipulation.

concepts.description: The bonds show power exchange, allowing different physical energy domains to share one modeling framework.

concepts.title: What inertial parameters describe
concepts.description: The force law needs mass, and the rotational law needs center-of-mass inertia; these finite moments characterize equivalent rigid-body inertial behavior, not a unique density field.

concepts.title: Linear-time recursive dynamics
concepts.description: Each pass visits each link once, so the work is c1 n+c2 n rather than a nested n-by-n calculation.

concepts.title: Terms represented by the model
concepts.description: The slide lists inertial, Coriolis, centrifugal and gravitational effects; fatigue behavior is not supplied by those rigid-body equations.

concepts.title: Force and center-of-mass acceleration
concepts.description: Multiply each acceleration component by the constant mass: F=(6,-3,0) N.

concepts.title: Euler moment and angular momentum
concepts.description: I_Cω is angular momentum, and its inertial rate includes the transport term ω×I_Cω.

concepts.title: When the gyroscopic term vanishes
concepts.description: The cross product is zero when angular momentum is parallel to angular velocity; this includes zero velocity, a principal axis or spherical inertia.

concepts.title: Inputs and output of inverse dynamics
concepts.description: Inverse dynamics computes the efforts required for a specified instantaneous trajectory state and robot model.
concepts.subtopic: Inputs and output of inverse dynamics

concepts.title: Outward and inward passes
concepts.description: The outward pass provides link accelerations and inertial loads; the inward pass then accumulates transmitted forces and moments.

concepts.title: Revolute angular-velocity propagation
concepts.description: The relative revolute motion adds qdot z=(0,0,3) to the inherited angular velocity.

concepts.title: Correcting the prismatic derivative mismatch
concepts.description: A prismatic joint contributes no relative angular motion, so angular acceleration is inherited through rotation; the printed right side is missing the time derivative.

concepts.title: Tangential and centripetal terms
concepts.description: Differentiating the offset velocity adds tangential acceleration α×p and centripetal acceleration ω×(ω×p).

concepts.title: Numerical center-of-mass acceleration
concepts.description: The tangential term is (0,1.5,0), the centripetal term is (-2,0,0), and adding a_O gives (-1,1.5,0).

concepts.title: Sliding-joint acceleration additions
concepts.description: The moving-point formula contributes a Coriolis term with factor 2 and the relative linear acceleration.

concepts.title: Center-of-mass frame convention
concepts.description: The slide uses a translated center-of-mass frame with the same orientation as the link frame.

concepts.title: Resultant and transmitted loads
concepts.description: The uppercase quantities follow Newton/Euler for the whole link; the lowercase quantities describe interlink transmission at the joint.

concepts.title: Why the distal force subtracts
concepts.description: Newton’s third law changes the distal action to its reaction; R changes its components into the current frame.

concepts.title: Moment arms about the center of mass
concepts.description: A moment arm starts at the chosen reference point, so subtract the mass-center position from each joint position.
concepts.subtopic: Moment arms about the center of mass

concepts.title: Inward force and moment recursion
concepts.description: The proximal moment balances the inertial moment, the distal transmitted moment and both moment-arm contributions in one common basis.

concepts.title: Revolute and prismatic effort
concepts.description: A rotational coordinate is driven by its axial moment, whereas a sliding coordinate is driven by its axial force.

concepts.title: Six-joint loop indices
concepts.description: Outward i=0 generates link 1 and i=5 generates link 6; inward then visits links 6 through 1.

concepts.title: A free terminal boundary
concepts.description: A free endpoint has no transmitted terminal load, but the last link still requires effort to produce its own acceleration.

concepts.title: Sign of the fictitious base acceleration
concepts.description: The fictitious acceleration is opposite the physical gravitational acceleration: a_0=-g_phys.
concepts.subtopic: Sign of the fictitious base acceleration

concepts.title: Physics prior and residual learning
concepts.description: The slide distinguishes using physical structure from learning residual errors, both of which can complement a nominal dynamics model.
